title: Policy 463.10 audit memoranda — transmittals to the Chief, native files, and version history
summary:
Seeks the records behind the monthly Policy 463.10 audit memoranda rather than the memoranda as previously produced, covering December 2025 through the date of production:

- Item 1: the email or other transmittal by which each memorandum was sent to the Chief of Police, together with the memorandum as attached at the time of transmittal.
- Item 2: records reflecting the Chief's review of each memorandum and its filing and retention.
- Item 3: the native word-processing file for each memorandum, as currently held.
- Item 4: any prior, superseded, draft, or alternate version, in any location.
- Item 5: system-maintained version history or file audit trail (M365, SharePoint, OneDrive, network file server) showing save events, dates, and associated account.
- Item 6: where the memoranda are filed and retained after the Chief's review.
- Item 7: any record reflecting a revision, correction, re-export, or re-issuance of any 463.10 memorandum.
- Item 8: the retention schedule applied to the memoranda and their prior versions.

A Scope paragraph expressly excludes the memorandum files already produced under W012461-040226 and W013260-081726, to foreclose an "already produced" deferral. Items are scoped uniformly across all memoranda from December 2025 forward rather than naming any single month.

policy_promises.quote: The audit shall be documented in the form of an internal department memorandum to the Chief of Police
policy_promises.tests: Whether a transmittal record exists for each memorandum, and what the memorandum contained at the moment it was sent to the Chief.

policy_promises.quote: After review by the Chief of Police, the memorandum and any associated documentation shall be filed and retained
policy_promises.tests: Whether the Chief's review left any record, where the memoranda are retained, and whether prior versions were retained as the retention obligation implies.

prior_pra_refs.note: Produced the April-July 2026 memoranda as PDF exports on 2026-08-20. Those files are expressly excluded from this request's scope.
Produced the December 2025 - March 2026 memoranda in native Microsoft Word (.doc) format on 2026-04-07. Those files are expressly excluded from this request's scope.
Produced an April 2026 memorandum on 2026-05-07 whose body text differs by one word from the April 2026 memorandum produced under W013260-081726. Deliberately not cited in the request text.

filed_because: The April 2026 audit memorandum was produced twice in materially different form: the copy produced under W012665-050426 (exported 2026-05-07 via Word for Microsoft 365) states the audit covered "usage for March 2026," while the copy produced under W013260-081726 (exported 2026-08-17 via Acrobat PDFMaker) states "usage for April 2026." Memo date, caption, and all other text are identical. PDF forensics establish that the change was made in the Word source and the file re-exported, not edited at the PDF layer, but they cannot date the edit — it falls somewhere in the 102 days between the two exports. Only the native file's metadata, the system version history, or the copy as transmitted to the Chief can date it. The request does not mention the discrepancy or name April, so that a response reporting no revisions stands on its own.
notes:
Filed 2026-08-24 15:24; 10-day statutory determination due 2026-09-03.

Items 1-3 are the substance: the transmitted copy is frozen at the moment it reached the Chief, so it is the reference version if the source was later edited. Item 5 is the only item that can date an edit directly.

Anticipate a Gov. Code section 7922.600 unusual-circumstances extension given items 1-5 span roughly nine memoranda; the severability clause is intended to limit that to the items that genuinely need it.
